properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From Anthony's VS Code work log (SOURCE: art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05, entries of 2026-10-05 at lines 350-354 and 376-387). The ideas, in the reporter's words: "a `loop_status` line 'repaired on open by vX: …'", and "append the first-open notice to `graph.server.log` (or keep `previous_reflow2_version` in `graph.meta.json`) under `--call` too, so the upgrade check can be done by whoever looks next".

THE FINDING THIS ANSWERS: fact:root-cause-every-one-shot-open-drops-the-version-verdict-and-the-repair-report-2026-10-05. Measured on 0.79.0: every one-shot open drops the verdict, the downgrade case included, and rewrites graph.meta.json either way. Its repair is reported only if the same process's call is loop_status. The 2026-09-28 walk (fact:root-cause-an-upgrade-under-a-session-is-known-at-open-and-said-only-to-stderr-2026-09-28) proposed keeping the verdict on the service and serving it in served_by. That reaches a live session. It cannot reach a one-shot door, where every call is a new process.

TWO QUESTIONS, ONE CLASS: what does the door SAY at the open (today, nothing), and what is KEPT for the next reader (today, only the usage ledger's client_version on door calls).

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) THE DOOR SAYS IT. Print the verdict on stderr, as the serving modes do, and carry `repaired_on_open` and `behind_record` in the reply of whatever tool the first call ran. Smallest, and the downgrade warning needs at least this. Lost when the process ends. SIZE: small.
(b) `previous_reflow2_version` (and the date it moved) GOES IN graph.meta.json. Additive to the stamp. But the stamp is compared whole (`was == now` decides Match), so that comparison must ignore the new field. SIZE: small to moderate.
(c) A SMALL APPEND-ONLY SIDECAR, such as `<graph>.opened.jsonl`: one line per version change, with the verdict, the type counts and the repair summary. Or append the same line to `graph.server.log` from every door, as the reporter asked (today that file is only the shared daemon's). SIZE: small.
(d) loop_status SERVES IT, read from (b) or (c), until acknowledged: "this store moved from 0.76.0 to 0.79.0 on <date>; additive; 2 retired values repaired". It reaches a door agent and a live session alike. Builds on (b) or (c). SIZE: moderate.
(e) NOTHING NEW. Document that `<graph>.usage.jsonl` already records `client_version` on each door call, so the version change can be read there. The verdict and the repair cannot. SIZE: doc only.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, kept beside it:
- `reflow2 read` is documented as changing nothing in the design or on disk. The open already rewrites graph.meta.json and repairs, and (c) would add one more write on a read. The owner may prefer to name the open's writes in that promise rather than add to them.
- fix/a-stores-identity-follows-its-real-path (in flight) is rewriting the same open path, and keeps an `identity_on_open` note the same way. A fix here should follow it, not race it.
- A note kept "until acknowledged" is one more line in a loop_status that is already long. In the field case the `head -40` problem was where lines sit, not how many there are.
- Every option is additive. None changes an existing field, so an MCP session that reads served_by today keeps working ("my brother likes using as is").

NOTHING IS PROMOTED.
properties.name: OPEN — should what a newer reflow2's first open of a store found and did (the version that last wrote it, the verdict, what it repaired) outlive the process that opened it, so whoever looks next can confirm the upgrade, on every door?
properties.rationale: Recorded as one open question for two field-log ideas (a loop_status line for the repair, and a durable record of the first-open notice), because measurement put both under one cause: the one-shot open drops what it learns. Under rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed. SOURCE: art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05.
